Resolves #21357

`examples/board/swimlanes` groups a product quarter's cards into one row per team (Design, Web, Mobile, Platform, then Unassigned) over the same five columns. It opens with Web folded. Every row header reads toggle, title and card count from its start and stays in view on a narrow board (#21394). A card dropped into another team's row takes that team, and both counts change. The record takes its cover (neomjs/pages#117), so the Task Board group publishes: 50 live examples in 19 groups.

Evidence: L3 (Chromium e2e at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844 in every theme the board ships, plus the catalog unit and Portal e2e pins) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-5, AC-7). AC-6's look sits outside CI. neomjs/pages#117 merged on 2026-11-19.

## Cold look

One fresh reader, given only the four frames, graded the swimlanes example 7/10. In their words, it shows "the same five columns per team ... in collapsible rows", and the subtitle tells them what to do. They read ▾/▸ as open and folded, and the badge as a card count, "but only because Design's column badges sum to 9". On the phone frame, the cut-off Ready column looks "like a bug", and the toggles and menu dots are "well under finger size". They saw the example as a sibling of `board/basic` rather than a superset: no WIP stripes and no table. The one change they would make is a larger chevron and "9 cards" instead of a bare "9".

Their points concern the board's lane header and the phone overflow, both engine surfaces this example uses as they are. They are noted as defect-notes, not changed here: the toggle's name lacks the lane's title and the count lacks a unit, and on a phone the cut-off next column gives no cue that the board scrolls sideways. WIP limits and the table are other candidates on #21346.
